themes_detail.label: Garbage Collection Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Missed Collection complaints spiked to 5 THIS WEEK versus a baseline average of 1.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 344% surge—signaling potential sanitation service failures affecting block-by-block refuse removal in Mott Haven/Melrose just as winter weather complicates street conditions.
evidence: 5 missed collection complaints THIS WEEK vs 1.1 weekly baseline (z-score: 3.68)
Timing coincides with winter weather pressures and street conditions
reporting_angles: Interview residents on specific blocks affected; map missed routes against scheduled collection days
Contact Sanitation Department to confirm staffing/vehicle availability constraints this week

themes_detail.label: Unlicensed Cannabis Retailers Proliferating
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis Retailer complaints exploded 1500% with 4 complaints filed 2 WEEKS AGO versus a baseline of 0.2 per week—the sharpest statistical spike across all categories (z-score: 8.66)—indicating rapid, uncontrolled expansion of illegal dispensaries in the district.
evidence: 4 cannabis retailer complaints 2 weeks ago vs 0.2 weekly baseline (z-score: 8.66, highest severity spike)
Suggests concentrated storefront activity in specific locations
reporting_angles: Geo-map the 4 complaints to identify street clusters; photograph storefront locations and compare to legal licensed retailer map
Interview NYPD enforcement units and State Liquor Authority on enforcement priorities and resource allocation for CD 201

themes_detail.label: Street Cleanliness Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Street Sweeping Complaints spiked to 11 filings 2 WEEKS AGO—a 633% surge from a baseline of 1.5 per week over 8 weeks (z-score: 6.72)—indicating neighborhood residents perceive degraded street conditions, potentially linked to missed collection issues and inadequate maintenance scheduling.
evidence: 11 street sweeping complaints 2 weeks ago vs 1.5 weekly baseline (z-score: 6.72)
Convergence signal: overlaps with missed collection spike, suggesting sanitation dept. capacity issue
reporting_angles: Walk affected neighborhoods with photos; cross-reference street sweeping schedules against complaint dates to identify skipped routes
Request Sanitation Department street-sweeping logs for past 4 weeks; interview residents on specific blocks

themes_detail.label: Encampment Complaints Double
themes_detail.summary: Homelessness-related Encampment complaints surged to 10 filings 2 WEEKS AGO—a 400% spike from a baseline of 2.0 per week (z-score: 4.28)—aligning with a recurring community board demand for expanded homeless services and suggesting concentrated tent/makeshift shelter activity.
evidence: 10 encampment complaints 2 weeks ago vs 2.0 weekly baseline (z-score: 4.28)
Community board has repeatedly requested expanded homeless services (standing budget request item)—unmet demand signal
reporting_angles: Geo-map the 10 encampment complaints to identify concentration zones; interview residents and unhoused individuals on root causes
Report on whether DHS shelter capacity in/near CD 201 is full; compare to community board homeless services requests over past 3 years

themes_detail.label: Police Non-Emergency Call Spike
themes_detail.summary: Non-Emergency Police Matter complaints jumped to 19 filings LAST WEEK—a 223% increase from a baseline of 5.9 per week (z-score: 5.81)—suggesting heightened resident demand for police response or intervention, possibly tied to concurrent encampment and unlicensed retail activity.
evidence: 19 non-emergency police complaints LAST WEEK vs 5.9 weekly baseline (z-score: 5.81)
Coincides with encampment spike (2 weeks ago) and cannabis retailer complaints (2 weeks ago)—possible convergence
reporting_angles: Request NYPD 311 summary data to identify category breakdown of non-emergency complaints (e.g., disorderly conduct, trespassing, suspected retail drug sales)
Cross-reference timing with encampment and cannabis complaints to determine whether single underlying issue or multiple concurrent crises
